crop.notes: Whole 'The Millers' article from headline to the closing rule; includes Arthur Chambers' challenge letter at the end.

ocr.notes: Gist and most names readable; many character errors, signatures (Ben Hogan, Tom Allen, Arthur Chambers) and some lines garbled or dropped.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat previewed the Allen-Hogan fight for $1,000 a side set for that day, reporting Allen already near the fight ground and both men in excellent condition, and reprinted the articles of agreement.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Tuesday, October 28, 1873'; masthead 'Daily Democrat'. Pre-1875 merger, so not the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen and Ben Hogan signed articles of agreement in St. Louis to fight for $1,000 a side under the new rules on October 28, 1873
Allen left St. Louis on Sunday for the vicinity of the fight ground ahead of the Hogan fight
Allen was to be seconded by Arthur Chambers and Patsy Curtin against Hogan; the steamer Continental was to carry spectators from the foot of Carr Street
Allen was to have a benefit at Deagle's Theater the night of the Hogan fight, with Hogan, Arthur Chambers and Young Ryan expected to spar
Allen's Washington Avenue saloon was crowded with betting on the eve of the Hogan fight, Allen the strong favorite

notes: Allen is said to have told the hack-driver he would 'put a terrible head on the bloody Dutchman' (reported speech, not a direct quote). Chambers' challenge to Mike Coburn is general boxing news, not recorded as a fact.
